# ATS Resume Checker

> A free, open source resume checker and builder. It reads a resume in the browser, compares it
> against a job posting, and exports a PDF that applicant tracking software parses correctly.
> There is no account, no database and no server: everything runs in the visitor's own tab.

## What it does

- Imports an existing resume from a PDF, extracting the text with pdf.js inside the browser.
- Shows a "parser view": the plain text an applicant tracking system extracts from the document,
  so a person can see the same thing the employer's software sees.
- Compares the resume against a pasted job posting, separates required from preferred terms using
  the posting's own headings and cues, and reports a match rate against the required set.
- Exports and re-imports the whole resume as JSON, so tailoring it to a new posting is quick.
- Prints to A4 through the browser, which keeps a real text layer in the PDF.

## Positions this project takes

- Hidden keywords in white text do not work and are not offered. Parsers strip styling and read the
  raw text layer, so the hidden block is visible to the recruiter, screening platforms flag the
  pattern, and a flagged application can be rejected with a fraud marker on the candidate record.
  The same applies to hidden instructions aimed at an AI screener.
- A missing keyword is reported as missing. The tool never adds a skill on a person's behalf.
- Two column resumes fail extraction because the parser reads the page in one pass and interleaves
  the columns, which is the most common reason a well written resume is rejected.
- Letter spacing on a heading survives into the PDF text layer and comes out as separated capitals
  that no parser recognises.
